## Overview
Deprecates the tracking blocker in favor of script loading allowing for
full control over what is blocked and what is not.
In the React packages, the script loader can also conditionally render
React components based on the consent. For example if you wanted to load
a script with `Next/Script` or a React Provider instead.

We now also have pre-defined scripts for stuff like Google Tag Manager,
Meta Pixel & Posthog

feat(react): add frame component to conditionally render iframes etc (#420)

## Overview
Core: 
Render iframes based on consent via data-src and data-category tags.
This does not display fallback content.

React: 
Conditionally render components & elements based on the consent. 

We do this in the UI level with react as you want a UI fallback for your
iFrames, to prevent layout shifts and provide better UX. This component
is customizable similar to the other c15t components.

This is useful for iframes such as for youtube embeds as they set
cookies on load or play.

## Related Issue
Fixes #335 

## Type of Change
- [x] 🚀 New feature

## Usage
c15t:
```html
  <iframe
    width="560"
    height="315"
    data-src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/mQJ6q1ZCzsg"
    data-category="marketing" // Note: Not typesafe
  />
```

@c15t/react:
``` tsx
<Frame category="marketing" className="h-[300px] w-[500px]">
	<iframe
		title="Cool Duck Video"
		src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/mQJ6q1ZCzsg"
		width="100%"
		height="100%"
	/>
</Frame>
```

feat(translations): add automated translations with Lingo.dev CLI (#500)

## Overview

This PR:

- adds support for more EU languages to the `@c15t/translations` package
- sets up [Lingo.dev CLI](https://lingo.dev/en/cli) for easier
generation and maintenance of translations

This approach has a few benefits:

- the translations are generated with AI
- as the source content is updated, only the changes are retranslated
- support additional languages with just a couple of (small) changes

Some other possible enhancements (not in this PR) include:

- translating the documentation (either for all locales or just a
subset)
- setting up CI/CD integration that:
    - verifies if translations have been generated
- commits translations automatically to repo (directly to the main
branch, or via PR, etc)

**Note:** Based on the config in this PR, a Lingo.dev API key is
required. It's also possible to BYOK with a standard LLM provider though
(e.g., OpenRouter).

## Related Issue

Fixes https://github.com/c15t/c15t/issues/497

This PR:

- adds support for more EU languages to the `@c15t/translations` package
- sets up [Lingo.dev CLI](https://lingo.dev/en/cli) for easier
generation and maintenance of translations

This approach has a few benefits:

- the translations are generated with AI
- as the source content is updated, only the changes are retranslated
- support additional languages with just a couple of (small) changes

Some other possible enhancements (not in this PR) include:

- translating the documentation (either for all locales or just a
subset)
- setting up CI/CD integration that:
    - verifies if translations have been generated
- commits translations automatically to repo (directly to the main
branch, or via PR, etc)

**Note:** Based on the config in this PR, a Lingo.dev API key is
required. It's also possible to BYOK with a standard LLM provider though
(e.g., OpenRouter).

refactor(workflows): consolidate and update deployment workflows (#538)

- Removed outdated workflows for canary, preview, and production
deployments.
- Introduced a new unified deployment workflow to handle various
deployment scenarios including PR previews, scheduled checks, and manual
triggers.
- Enhanced the release workflow to support both canary and regular
releases with appropriate configurations for pnpm and Node.js.
- Improved permissions and concurrency settings for better workflow
management.
## Overview

This PR consolidates and enhances GitHub Actions workflows to improve
maintainability and add new capabilities:

1. **Merged release workflows**: Combined `canary-release.yml` and
`release.yml` into a single unified workflow that handles both canary
and production releases based on branch triggers.

2. **Added PR preview workflow**: Created a new workflow
(`pr-preview.yml`) that automatically detects changed packages in PRs
and publishes preview versions to `pkg.pr.new` for testing before
merging.

3. **Merged docs deployment workflows**: Combined
`deploy-docs-preview.yml` and `deploy-docs-production.yml` into a single
workflow with manual trigger support for both preview and production
deployments.

**Benefits:**
- Reduced workflow duplication and maintenance overhead
- Single source of truth for release and deployment logic
- Better developer experience with PR preview packages
- Manual deployment controls for production/preview environments
- Simplified npm trusted publisher configuration (only one workflow file
needed)

## Related Issue

Fixes # (issue)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🏗️ Refactor (no functional changes)
- [x] ✨ Enhancement (improves existing functionality)
- [x] 🚀 New feature

## Implementation Details

### Key Changes

1. **Unified Release Workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)
   - Merged `canary-release.yml` and `release.yml` into single workflow
   - Triggers on push to `main` or `canary` branches
   - Uses conditional steps to handle canary vs production releases
   - Maintains all existing functionality while reducing duplication

2. **PR Preview Workflow** (`.github/workflows/pr-preview.yml`)
   - New workflow for publishing preview packages from PRs
   - Automatically detects which packages changed in PR
   - Only publishes packages with `publishConfig` (published packages)
- Security: Only runs for repository members or PRs with
`deploy:preview` label
   - Publishes to `pkg.pr.new` with version `0.0.0-preview.<SHA>`
   - Adds install instructions as PR notices

3. **Unified Docs Deployment Workflow**
(`.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`)
   - Merged `deploy-docs-preview.yml` and `deploy-docs-production.yml`
   - Supports automatic deployments on push to `main`/`canary`
   - Added manual `workflow_dispatch` trigger with options:
     - Deployment type: `preview` or `production`
     - Branch selection
     - PR number (for preview deployments)
   - Conditional steps based on deployment type

### Technical Notes

- **Release workflow**: Uses conditional steps with `if` conditions to
determine canary vs production behavior, avoiding duplicate code while
maintaining clear separation of concerns.

- **PR preview workflow**: Uses matrix strategy to build/publish
multiple changed packages in parallel. Package detection uses git diff
to identify changed packages and filters to only published packages.

- **Docs deployment workflow**: Uses a deployment info extraction step
to determine branch/PR context, then conditionally runs preview or
production deployment steps based on trigger type.

- **Workflow consolidation**: All merged workflows maintain backward
compatibility - existing triggers and behaviors continue to work as
before.

feat(backend): add OTel instrumentation and strip PII from spans (#582)

## Overview
feat(backend): add OTel instrumentation and strip PII from spans

Instrument DB, cache, external, and request operations with
OpenTelemetry
   spans and metrics across handlers, registries, and the GVL resolver.
Strip PII from span attributes by removing error.message, error.stack,
   and http.path; sanitize external URLs to drop query params; and use
hostname-only span names for external calls. Consolidate error handling
   into a shared exported handleSpanError function.

Add e2e test with real InMemorySpanExporter that enforces an attribute
key allowlist and blocks PII value patterns (IPs, emails, stack traces,
   query strings) across all span types.

refactor(core): rename gdprTypes to consentCategories, add debug logger, remove hardcoded  necessary checks (#584)

## Overview
Replace GDPR-specific naming with generic consent vocabulary throughout
the core package so the config works for any consent category, not just
GDPR presets. Add a gated debug logger (disabled by default) that
replaces bare console.log calls, and make save-consents use the
ConsentType config properties (disabled, defaultValue) instead of
checking for the literal string 'necessary'

saveConsents was mutating the consents object in place and setting the
same reference back. Now it spreads into a new object ({ ...consents }),
so he reference always changes.

has, hasConsented, getDisplayedConsents are wrapped in useCallback with
reactive deps like [consents]. When the consents reference changes,
useCallback returns a new function reference. React Compiler caches
based on function identity.

fix(react): react compiler compatability (#605)

## Overview
saveConsents was mutating the consents object in place and setting the
same reference back. Now it spreads into a new object ({ ...consents }),
so he reference always changes.

has, hasConsented, getDisplayedConsents are wrapped in useCallback with
reactive deps like [consents]. When the consents reference changes,
useCallback returns a new function reference. React Compiler caches
based on function identity.

hostname-only span names for external calls. Consolidate error handling

fix(react): react compiler compatability (#605)

## Overview
saveConsents was mutating the consents object in place and setting the
same reference back. Now it spreads into a new object ({ ...consents }),
so he reference always changes.

has, hasConsented, getDisplayedConsents are wrapped in useCallback with
reactive deps like [consents]. When the consents reference changes,
useCallback returns a new function reference. React Compiler caches
based on function identity.

fix: add NODE_AUTH_TOKEN for npm publish auth (#686)

## Summary

- Adds `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env var (set to `NPM_RELEASE_TOKEN` secret) to
all three release steps (production, canary, RC)
- Fixes the E404 errors that caused all 7 packages to fail publishing at
v1.8.6

## Root Cause

`actions/setup-node@v4` with `registry-url` creates an `.npmrc` at
`$RUNNER_TEMP` that references `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`, and sets
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` to point to it. The changesets action creates
`~/.npmrc` using `${NPM_TOKEN}`, but npm **ignores** it because
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` takes precedence.

Since the workflow only set `NPM_TOKEN` (not `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`), npm was
authenticating with an empty token — resulting in E404 for all publish
attempts.

The previous `npm install -g npm@latest` step (removed in #684) likely
reset the npm config chain, masking this issue. Once that step was
removed, auth broke.

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge to main → release workflow re-runs → 1.8.6 publishes
successfully to npm
- [ ] Verify `npm view @c15t/backend@1.8.6` returns package info after
publish

## Overview
feat(backend): add OTel instrumentation and strip PII from spans

Instrument DB, cache, external, and request operations with
OpenTelemetry
   spans and metrics across handlers, registries, and the GVL resolver.
Strip PII from span attributes by removing error.message, error.stack,
   and http.path; sanitize external URLs to drop query params; and use
hostname-only span names for external calls. Consolidate error handling
   into a shared exported handleSpanError function.

Add e2e test with real InMemorySpanExporter that enforces an attribute
key allowlist and blocks PII value patterns (IPs, emails, stack traces,
   query strings) across all span types.

fix(react): react compiler compatability (#605)

## Overview
saveConsents was mutating the consents object in place and setting the
same reference back. Now it spreads into a new object ({ ...consents }),
so he reference always changes.

has, hasConsented, getDisplayedConsents are wrapped in useCallback with
reactive deps like [consents]. When the consents reference changes,
useCallback returns a new function reference. React Compiler caches
based on function identity.

Fixes #604

feat: policy packs (#637) - Added policy packs for flexible backends, no hard coded values - Improved support for headless components > [!NOTE] > ### Add policy packs for jurisdiction-aware consent resolution with snapshot signing and offline fallback > - Introduces a `PolicyConfig`/policy pack system where ordered packs of rules are matched by country/region to produce a `ResolvedPolicy` with model, UI hints, categories, and proof settings; unmatched packs fall back to a `no_banner` policy. > - The `/init` route resolves a policy decision per request, creates a signed JWT snapshot token (`policySnapshotToken`), and gates IAB fields (GVL, translations) on the resolved model being `iab`. > - The `POST /subjects` handler verifies the snapshot token at write time, enforces policy category scope (strict/permissive), applies purpose allowlists, and persists a deduplicated `runtimePolicyDecision` record linked to each consent row. > - The client store detects material policy fingerprint changes and resets stored consent when the active policy changes, and seeds `policyBanner`/`policyDialog` UI hints into state. > - React components (`ConsentBanner`, `ConsentWidget`, `IABConsentBanner`, `IABConsentDialog`) now render only policy-allowed actions in policy-determined order/layout via new `useHeadlessConsentUI` and `useHeadlessIABConsentUI` hooks. > - Adds `policyPackPresets` with regional defaults (Europe opt-in/IAB, California opt-in/opt-out, Quebec opt-in, world no-banner) and a CLI codemod `offline-add-policy-packs` to inject starter packs into existing offline configs. > - DevTools gains a dedicated Policy tab showing resolved policy identity, UI surface config, proof settings, and match trace; the Location panel and panel footer show init source metadata. > - Risk: `POST /subjects` returns HTTP 400 for disallowed categories in strict scope mode, and stored consent is silently reset when the material policy fingerprint changes. > > > > Macroscope summarized 3dddfa6. > > --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6

## Main thread impact

### Before: style injection blocks the main thread

```
Main thread ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  │ Parse JS (435 KB, includes 244 KB CSS strings)
  │ Execute JS
  │   ├─ createElement("style") × 9    ← synchronous DOM mutation
  │   ├─ textContent = "..." × 9       ← 244 KB of CSS strings
  │   ├─ head.appendChild() × 9        ← triggers style recalc each time
  │   └─ style recalculation × 9       ← browser recomputes all styles
  │ React render
  │ First styled paint                  ← styles only available AFTER JS runs
  ▼
```

### After: CSS loads off the main thread

```
Main thread ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  │ Parse JS (361 KB, no CSS strings)   ← 74 KB less to parse
  │ Execute JS                          ← no DOM mutations for styles
  │ React render
  │ First styled paint
  ▼
Network ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  │ Fetch styles.css (7.4 KB gzip)     ← parallel with JS, off main thread
  │ Parse CSS (native engine)           ← ~10x faster than JS string→DOM
  │ Single style recalculation          ← one pass, not 9
  ▼
```

from test jobs (turbo remote cache handles deduplication), adds bun
install + Playwright browser caching via a reusable composite action,
introduces path filtering to skip CI on docs-only changes, and adds
concurrency control to cancel stale PR runs. Bun is pinned to `1.3.11`
across all workflows to match the `packageManager` field.

encapsulates bun setup, dependency caching (`~/.bun/install/cache`),
`bun install`, and optional Playwright browser caching
(`~/.cache/ms-playwright`)

all jobs now run in parallel after a lightweight `changes` gate. Turbo

fix: resolve npm auth and upgrade issues in release workflow (#695)

## Overview

Ports the release workflow fixes from `main` to the `2.0.0` branch. The
release workflow was failing due to two issues: Node.js 22.22.2's
bundled npm has a corrupted `promise-retry` module that breaks `npm
install -g`, and `actions/setup-node`'s `.npmrc` uses `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`
(not `NPM_TOKEN`), causing E404 publish errors.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Implementation Details

### Key Changes
1. **Fixed npm upgrade order** — moved npm upgrade step before `bun
install` and added a `promise-retry` workaround for Node.js 22.22.2's
broken bundled npm
2. **Added `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`** to all three release steps (canary, RC,
production) — `actions/setup-node`'s `.npmrc` uses this env var via
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, taking precedence over `NPM_TOKEN`
3. **Updated bun-version** from pinned `1.3.11` to `latest`

### Technical Notes
- `actions/setup-node@v4` with `registry-url` creates an `.npmrc`
referencing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. This config takes precedence via
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, so setting only `NPM_TOKEN` resulted in an
empty auth token.
- The old `npm install -g npm@latest` step was placed after `bun
install` and would fail on Node.js 22.22.2 due to a missing
`promise-retry` dependency. The fix installs `promise-retry` globally
first (with error suppression) before upgrading npm.

feat: simplify static prefetch consumption before 2.0 GA (#712)

## Overview
Replace the RC static-prefetch consumer flow with automatic
request-context matching so static routes only need to start `/init`
early while dynamic SSR continues to use `fetchInitialData()` unchanged.
This adds canonical request-context metadata to SSR and browser-prefetch
payloads, auto-consumes matching prefetched data during first hosted
store initialization, and updates docs/templates/examples to the smaller
GA API surface.

## Related Issue
Fixes #711

## Type of Change
- [x] ✨ Enhancement (improves existing functionality)
- [x] 📚 Documentation
- [x] 🏗️ Refactor (no functional changes)
- [x] ⚡ Performance

## Implementation Details
### Key Changes
1. Added request-context metadata and matching helpers for SSR and
browser-prefetch payloads, including canonical backend URL handling and
ambient GPC checks.
2. Switched hosted runtime initialization to auto-consume matching
prefetched data on first store creation, and changed SSR reuse to skip
only on `context_mismatch` instead of any override.
3. Removed the public RC prefetch consumer exports and updated docs,
templates, and benchmark/example providers to the automatic model.

### Before / After
Static route setup no longer needs a separate consumer API in the
provider.

```tsx
// Before
import { ConsentManagerProvider, getPrefetchedInitialData } from '@c15t/nextjs';

<ConsentManagerProvider
  options={{
    mode: 'hosted',
    backendURL: '/api/c15t',
    ssrData: getPrefetchedInitialData({
      backendURL: '/api/c15t',
      overrides: { country: 'DE', region: 'BE', language: 'de' },
    }),
  }}
/>

// After
import { ConsentManagerProvider } from '@c15t/nextjs';

<ConsentManagerProvider
  options={{
    mode: 'hosted',
    backendURL: '/api/c15t',
    overrides: { country: 'DE', region: 'BE', language: 'de' },
  }}
/>
```

SSR-prefetched data is now reused when the effective request context
matches instead of being invalidated by any override.

```ts
// Before
if (!ssrData || get().overrides) {
  set({ ssrDataUsed: false, ssrSkippedReason: 'no_data' });
  return undefined;
}

// After
if (!ssrData) {
  set({ ssrDataUsed: false, ssrSkippedReason: 'no_data' });
  return undefined;
}

if (data?.init && !shouldReuseSSRData(config, data)) {
  set({ ssrDataUsed: false, ssrSkippedReason: 'context_mismatch' });
  return undefined;
}
```

### Technical Notes
Dynamic SSR stays explicit and unchanged; browser-prefetch reuse is
internal-only and first-initialization-only, so cached runtimes do not
adopt newly discovered prefetched data later.

- Introduces manifest step types for `loadScript`, `setGlobal`,
`callGlobal`, `pushToDataLayer`, and `inlineScript`
- Splits manifest handling into compile and runtime phases:
- `compileManifest()` interpolates config and normalizes install/setup
artifacts
- `resolvedManifestToScript()` converts the resolved manifest into
runtime `Script` objects and lifecycle hooks
- Supports consent signaling for Google Consent Mode style integrations
via manifest metadata

resolves for the same manifest + config reuse the compiled manifest
- Keeps the manifest architecture while reducing repeated compile
overhead on hot paths
- Preserves room for targeted imperative overrides where a vendor needs
a more specialized runtime path

Moves policy-driven action resolution utilities into `c15t` core so
non-React runtimes can share the same logic:

Fi branding sizing across host pages (#730)

## Overview
The prebuilt consent surfaces treated the INTH full logo differently
from the c15t wordmark, which left the raw `svg` exposed to host-page
CSS and caused it to either balloon or collapse in consumer apps. This
change wraps the INTH wordmark in the shared internal container and adds
explicit sizing rules on the wrapper and nested `svg`, so the stock
branding path stays stable across docs, marketing pages, and other
embedded shells.

## Related Issue
Fixes #719

1. Wrap the INTH full logo in the shared LTR wordmark container in
`@c15t/react` so it uses the same internal structure as the c15t
branding path.
2. Add explicit flex, max-width, display, and aspect-ratio rules in
`@c15t/ui` so host-page `svg` rules cannot blow up or collapse the INTH
logo.

`@c15t/nextjs` is included because its styled surfaces consume the same
React/UI branding path and should ship aligned package versions with the
CSS hardening.

fix: add NODE_AUTH_TOKEN for npm publish auth (#686)

## Summary

- Adds `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` env var (set to `NPM_RELEASE_TOKEN` secret) to
all three release steps (production, canary, RC)
- Fixes the E404 errors that caused all 7 packages to fail publishing at
v1.8.6

## Root Cause

`actions/setup-node@v4` with `registry-url` creates an `.npmrc` at
`$RUNNER_TEMP` that references `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`, and sets
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` to point to it. The changesets action creates
`~/.npmrc` using `${NPM_TOKEN}`, but npm **ignores** it because
`NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` takes precedence.

Since the workflow only set `NPM_TOKEN` (not `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`), npm was
authenticating with an empty token — resulting in E404 for all publish
attempts.

The previous `npm install -g npm@latest` step (removed in #684) likely
reset the npm config chain, masking this issue. Once that step was
removed, auth broke.

successfully to npm

Harden CI supply chain security (#853)

## Summary

This hardens the repository against the GitHub Actions cache-poisoning
and privileged-PR workflow class described in the May 2026 TanStack
incident.

Changes include:
- remove the docs deploy workflow
- replace remaining `pull_request_target` usage with safer PR/workflow
patterns
- prevent PR jobs from receiving Turbo remote-cache credentials
- replace write-capable cache usage with restore-only cache usage where
cache writes are not needed
- remove long-lived npm publish token env vars from release jobs so
publishing relies on OIDC trusted publishing
- pin third-party GitHub Actions and CI tools to fixed versions or
commit SHAs
- add a zizmor GitHub Actions security workflow
- add Bun install cooldown settings via `bunfig.toml`
- require CODEOWNERS review for `.github/` changes from both core
maintainers
- add `SECURITY_HARDENING.md` as a reusable guide and prompt for
bringing other OSS repos to the same baseline

## Validation

- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; Dir[".github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}",
".github/actions/*/action.yml"].each { |f| YAML.load_file(f) }; puts
"workflow yaml ok"'`
- `rg` risky-pattern scan for privileged PR workflows, write caches, npm
token env vars, direct Turbo secret env in PR jobs, floating Bun/tool
versions: no matches
- `rg` action-ref scan for non-SHA third-party action refs: no matches
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile --dry-run --ignore-scripts`

## Follow-up Admin Settings

After merge, confirm npm trusted publishing is configured for every
published package, remove stale npm publish secrets from repository/org
settings, and make CODEOWNERS plus the GitHub Actions security workflow
required in branch protection or rulesets.

feat(translations): add automated translations with Lingo.dev CLI (#500)

This PR:

- adds support for more EU languages to the `@c15t/translations` package
- sets up [Lingo.dev CLI](https://lingo.dev/en/cli) for easier
generation and maintenance of translations

This approach has a few benefits:

- the translations are generated with AI
- as the source content is updated, only the changes are retranslated
- support additional languages with just a couple of (small) changes

Some other possible enhancements (not in this PR) include:

- translating the documentation (either for all locales or just a
subset)
- setting up CI/CD integration that:
    - verifies if translations have been generated
- commits translations automatically to repo (directly to the main
branch, or via PR, etc)

**Note:** Based on the config in this PR, a Lingo.dev API key is
required. It's also possible to BYOK with a standard LLM provider though
(e.g., OpenRouter).

Fixes https://github.com/c15t/c15t/issues/497

refactor(workflows): consolidate and update deployment workflows (#538)

- Removed outdated workflows for canary, preview, and production
deployments.
- Introduced a new unified deployment workflow to handle various
deployment scenarios including PR previews, scheduled checks, and manual
triggers.
- Enhanced the release workflow to support both canary and regular
releases with appropriate configurations for pnpm and Node.js.
- Improved permissions and concurrency settings for better workflow
management.
## Overview

This PR consolidates and enhances GitHub Actions workflows to improve
maintainability and add new capabilities:

1. **Merged release workflows**: Combined `canary-release.yml` and
`release.yml` into a single unified workflow that handles both canary
and production releases based on branch triggers.

2. **Added PR preview workflow**: Created a new workflow
(`pr-preview.yml`) that automatically detects changed packages in PRs
and publishes preview versions to `pkg.pr.new` for testing before
merging.

3. **Merged docs deployment workflows**: Combined
`deploy-docs-preview.yml` and `deploy-docs-production.yml` into a single
workflow with manual trigger support for both preview and production
deployments.

**Benefits:**
- Reduced workflow duplication and maintenance overhead
- Single source of truth for release and deployment logic
- Better developer experience with PR preview packages
- Manual deployment controls for production/preview environments
- Simplified npm trusted publisher configuration (only one workflow file
needed)

## Related Issue

Fixes # (issue)

## Type of Change

- [x] 🏗️ Refactor (no functional changes)
- [x] ✨ Enhancement (improves existing functionality)
- [x] 🚀 New feature

## Implementation Details

### Key Changes

1. **Unified Release Workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)
   - Merged `canary-release.yml` and `release.yml` into single workflow
   - Triggers on push to `main` or `canary` branches
   - Uses conditional steps to handle canary vs production releases
   - Maintains all existing functionality while reducing duplication

2. **PR Preview Workflow** (`.github/workflows/pr-preview.yml`)
   - New workflow for publishing preview packages from PRs
   - Automatically detects which packages changed in PR
   - Only publishes packages with `publishConfig` (published packages)
- Security: Only runs for repository members or PRs with
`deploy:preview` label
   - Publishes to `pkg.pr.new` with version `0.0.0-preview.<SHA>`
   - Adds install instructions as PR notices

3. **Unified Docs Deployment Workflow**
(`.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`)
   - Merged `deploy-docs-preview.yml` and `deploy-docs-production.yml`
   - Supports automatic deployments on push to `main`/`canary`
   - Added manual `workflow_dispatch` trigger with options:
     - Deployment type: `preview` or `production`
     - Branch selection
     - PR number (for preview deployments)
   - Conditional steps based on deployment type

### Technical Notes

- **Release workflow**: Uses conditional steps with `if` conditions to
determine canary vs production behavior, avoiding duplicate code while
maintaining clear separation of concerns.

- **PR preview workflow**: Uses matrix strategy to build/publish
multiple changed packages in parallel. Package detection uses git diff
to identify changed packages and filters to only published packages.

- **Docs deployment workflow**: Uses a deployment info extraction step
to determine branch/PR context, then conditionally runs preview or
production deployment steps based on trigger type.

- **Workflow consolidation**: All merged workflows maintain backward
compatibility - existing triggers and behaviors continue to work as
before.

feat(backend): add OTel instrumentation and strip PII from spans (#582)

## Overview
feat(backend): add OTel instrumentation and strip PII from spans

Instrument DB, cache, external, and request operations with
OpenTelemetry
   spans and metrics across handlers, registries, and the GVL resolver.
Strip PII from span attributes by removing error.message, error.stack,
   and http.path; sanitize external URLs to drop query params; and use
hostname-only span names for external calls. Consolidate error handling
   into a shared exported handleSpanError function.

Add e2e test with real InMemorySpanExporter that enforces an attribute
key allowlist and blocks PII value patterns (IPs, emails, stack traces,
   query strings) across all span types.

refactor(core): rename gdprTypes to consentCategories, add debug logger, remove hardcoded  necessary checks (#584)

## Overview
Replace GDPR-specific naming with generic consent vocabulary throughout
the core package so the config works for any consent category, not just
GDPR presets. Add a gated debug logger (disabled by default) that
replaces bare console.log calls, and make save-consents use the
ConsentType config properties (disabled, defaultValue) instead of
checking for the literal string 'necessary'

## Overview
saveConsents was mutating the consents object in place and setting the
same reference back. Now it spreads into a new object ({ ...consents }),
so he reference always changes.

has, hasConsented, getDisplayedConsents are wrapped in useCallback with
reactive deps like [consents]. When the consents reference changes,
useCallback returns a new function reference. React Compiler caches
based on function identity.
